24.original: Get the captivated courier's attention with a /poke.

48.original: Oh, hello there. You're an adventurer, right? Can I interest you in a job?

49.original: We're supposed to send out a shipment of electrope today, but the courier in charge appears to be taking her sweet time.

50.original: If our shipment falls behind schedule, it will bring Everkeep's factories to a screeching halt. I have to stay and handle things here, so could you go and tell the courier she has a job to do, please?

51.original: Given her obsession with technology, like as not, you'll find her wherever there's a clear view of the bucket elevator. She may not hear you approach, so give her a <hex:024804F201F403><hex:024904F201F503>poke<hex:0249020103><hex:0248020103> if you need to.

52.original: The courier I speak of tends to linger in places where there's a clear view of the bucket elevator. She may not hear you approach, so give her a <hex:024804F201F403><hex:024904F201F503>poke<hex:0249020103><hex:0248020103> if you need to.

54.original: The captivated courier does not appear to have noticed you. Perhaps a small <hex:024804F201F403><hex:024904F201F503>poke<hex:0249020103><hex:0248020103> will get her attention.

56.original: Ah, you're here about the delivery─oh gods, the <hex:021A020203>delivery<hex:021A020103>! I was so enraptured watching the elevator that I must have lost track of time. Again...

57.original: I admit, I never get sick of seeing it in action. The hover cargo we use is great and all, but I mean, it can't possibly compare to the sheer <hex:021A020203>scale<hex:021A020103> of─

58.original: Gah, no, I can't start rambling now! Sorry, but I'd better get back to work!

59.original: Thanks for the assistance. Much as I can appreciate a fellow enthusiast of our technology, I can't allow it to impact our work.

60.original: The electrope we excavate here is a lifeline for Everkeep, and I do mean that quite literally.

61.original: This precious resource is used to create all manner of things, from daily necessities to heavy machinery, so you can imagine how a single hitch in the supply chain risks a ripple effect of chaos.

62.original: At any rate, here's a little something for your trouble.
